GK-02.c01: **Disqualified** ("lose your CDL") means you may not drive a CMV for a set time, or for life.
A **conviction** means a court finds you guilty; **BAC** is blood alcohol concentration, the percent of alcohol in your blood.
Most disqualification periods in this lesson are **minimums** ("at least").
GK-02.c02: Disqualified for **any reason** → you may not drive a CMV.
Most disqualification periods are **minimums** ("at least"), and some last for life.
GK-02.c03: Driving a CMV with a BAC of **.04 percent or more** is illegal, because even a little alcohol slows your reactions.
Any measurable alcohol below .04 → **out of service for 24 hours**.
Major offenses (alcohol, drugs, test refusal, leaving the scene, CMV felony, driving suspended, fatal negligence) → CDL lost **at least 1 year** first time.
First major offense in a CMV **placarded for HazMat** → at least **3 years**; a 2nd major offense → life.
Using a CMV for a felony involving **controlled substances** → **life**, even the first time; refusing a test counts like driving drunk (implied consent).
GK-02.c04: Serious violations include speeding **15 mph or more** over the limit, reckless driving, erratic lane changes, following too closely, and driving without the correct CDL.
2 serious violations in a CMV within **3 years** → at least **60 days**.
3 or more within 3 years → at least **120 days**.
One serious violation alone brings **no disqualification**, because it takes repeats to show a risky pattern.
GK-02.c05: An **out-of-service order** means you or your vehicle may not drive for a set time or until a problem is fixed.
Driving anyway → 1st at least **90 days**, 2nd within 10 years at least **1 year**, 3rd or more within 10 years at least 3 years.
Repeats are counted over a **10-year** window, not the usual 3 years.
Federal rules say 180 days / 2 years / 3 years, but answer the handbook's **90 days / 1 year / 3 years** on the test.
GK-02.c06: Railroad crossing violations → 1st at least **60 days**, 2nd within 3 years at least **120 days**, 3rd within 3 years at least 1 year.
Unlike serious violations, the **first** railroad violation already costs 60 days, because a train cannot stop quickly.
There are **6 offenses**; drivers not required to always stop must stop when tracks are not clear and must slow to check for trains.
Drivers who must always stop (for example all passenger and HazMat vehicles) break the rule by **not stopping** before going onto the crossing.
All drivers → need **room to get all the way across** without stopping, obey signals or officers, and avoid getting stuck from low clearance.
GK-02.c07: An **H** endorsement requires **fingerprints** and a background check.
You are denied or lose it if you lack lawful permanent resident status, renounce U.S. citizenship, or are wanted, indicted or convicted for certain felonies.
Being judged to lack mental capacity or being involuntarily committed also disqualifies you, as does the **TSA** judging you a security threat.
The check exists because hazardous materials could be used to harm many people.
GK-02.c08: Under the **MCSIA of 1999**, certain moving violations in your own car can cost your CMV driving privilege.
Car privilege suspended, revoked or cancelled for **traffic-law** violations (not parking) → your **CDL privilege is lost too**.
Car privilege lost for **alcohol, controlled substances or a felony** → CDL lost **1 year**; a second such violation, car or CMV → life.
You **cannot get a hardship license** to drive a CMV, because habits in a car come with you into a truck.
GK-02.c09: [CA] Record retention → major **55 years**, out-of-service **15**, accidents and serious violations 10, railroad 4, minor 3.
[CA] An accident you caused = **1 point**; reckless driving, hit-and-run or DUI = **2 points**.
[CA] A violation in a CMV counts **1½ times** its points, because the same mistake is more dangerous in a heavy vehicle.
[CA] **Negligent operator** → **4 points in 12 months**, 6 in 24 months, or 8 in 36 months.
[CA] After a hearing: **6, 8 or 10** points (not if earned in a Class C car); Class A/B without a special certificate or endorsement: **2 extra points**.
GK-02.c10: [CA] The hands-free and texting penalties apply to your CDL **in any vehicle**, your own car included.
[CA] 2nd violation within 3 years → at least **60 days** + **1 point**.
[CA] 3rd or later within 3 years → at least **120 days** + 1 point, because a phone takes your eyes, hands and attention off the road.
GK-02.c11: Major offense → **1 year** (3 years if HazMat placarded), 2nd → **life**; a controlled-substance felony using a CMV → life at once.
Serious violations within 3 years → **60 days** for 2, **120 days** for 3 or more.
Out-of-service violations over **10 years** → **90 days / 1 year / 3 years**; railroad over 3 years → 60 days / 120 days / 1 year.
[CA] Hands-free/texting in any vehicle → 2nd **60 days + 1 point**, 3rd **120 days + 1 point**.
Car suspension for alcohol, drugs or felony → **1 year**, second → **life**; measurable alcohol under .04 → 24 hours out of service.
